subject.title: Exec/tool failures show "(see attached image)" and suppress model response

question: Should non-mutating exec/bash failures with no user-facing reply produce a compact warning or incomplete-turn fallback, and how should that interact with current side-effect, delivery, and recoverable-error suppression guards?
rationale: Current source proves the remaining silent path, but changing it is terminal-policy behavior that can trade user-visible silence for warning noise or unsafe recovery semantics.

options.title: Adopt compact no-reply warning
options.body: Show a compact exec/bash failure warning or incomplete-turn fallback only when no user-facing reply or delivery evidence exists, while preserving existing suppression for acknowledged, delivered, recoverable, or side-effectful paths.

options.title: Keep current suppression
options.body: Accept that non-mutating exec-like failures can remain silent in normal chat turns to avoid warning noise, then document or close the remaining policy as intentional.

options.title: Require live channel repro first
options.body: Hold code changes until a maintainer or reporter captures a current Discord, Slack, or Telegram repro that still shows the silent no-reply path after the beta placeholder fixes.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact no-reply warning
recommendation.body: Show a compact exec/bash failure warning or incomplete-turn fallback only when no user-facing reply or delivery evidence exists, while preserving existing suppression for acknowledged, delivered, recoverable, or side-effectful paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history signal for the terminal-classifier and incomplete-turn policy area that this decision would change.
